newsitem.title: UK: UK Liberal Democrats adopt carbon tax plan.
newsitem.headline: UK Liberal Democrats adopt carbon tax plan.

text.p: Britain's minority Liberal Democrats on Monday adopted a proposal for a carbon tax and a major programme of investment in energy conservation paid for by supply companies to reduce British energy consumption.
A motion adopted at the party's annual conference said the plan could help to reduce carbon dioxide emissions by two percent a year.

Environment spokesman Matthew Taylor said the carbon tax would be brought in gradually, and would fund cuts in value added tax and employer's National Insurance payments, which he called "jobs' taxes".
"There are many who still argue that we cannot afford to protect the environment," Taylor said. "That is a myth."

Lord Derek Ezra, former chairman of Britain's National Coal Board, told the conference that diverting the current nuclear fuel levy to a new Energy Savings Trust could help to provide it with one billion stg a year.
It could use the money to invest in non-fossil fuel sources and the development of clean coal technology, he said.

In a separate motion, the party also called for a two percent levy on water companies' profits to fund grants and interest free loans to households and small firms undertaking water conservation measures.
